Klasse Bucket<A>

java.lang.Object
org.quurz.foomp.base.util.Bucket<A>
Typparameter:
A - element type accepted by this bucket
public class Bucket<A> extends Object

A simple in-memory batching buffer with overflow behaviour (“bucket”). Elements are accumulated until the configured maximum size is reached; then the batch is flushed to a provided sink, the bucket is emptied, and accumulation continues.

Intended use cases:

  • Event/callback pipelines where items arrive one-by-one and should be processed in batches.
  • Batching for sinks like databases, file/IO, message queues, or HTTP endpoints.
  • Non-streaming scenarios where you want explicit add()/flush() control.

Notes and guidance:

  • For stream pipelines on recent JDKs, prefer java.util.stream.Gatherers.windowFixed(int) for size-based chunking.
  • Thread-safety: this implementation uses a write lock around mutation and flush. The current design invokes the sink while holding the write lock. If the sink is slow or blocking, consider adapting the implementation to copy-and-release the lock before calling the sink.
  • Memory: the buffer grows up to maxSize. There is no time-based flushing in this class.
  • Future extensions (not implemented here): size-or-time flushing, retry policies on sink failures, dead-letter sinks, asynchronous sinks with bounded parallelism, metrics hooks.

1.0.0

  • Methodendetails

    • bucket

      public static <A> Bucket<A> bucket(int maxSize, @NonNull Consumer<List<A>> sink)

      Creates a new Bucket.

      Contract:

      • maxSize must be at least 1.
      • sink must not be null and must tolerate being called multiple times, possibly with empty lists if used incorrectly.
      Typparameter:
      A - the element type
      Parameter:
      maxSize - the maximum number of elements per batch; must be >= 1
      sink - the consumer invoked on flush with the current batch; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      a new Bucket<A>
      Löst aus:
      IllegalArgumentException - if maxSize < 1
      NullPointerException - if sink == null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • toBucket

      public static <A> Collector<A,List<A>,Nothing> toBucket(int maxSize, @NonNull Consumer<List<A>> sink)

      Creates a Collector that routes stream elements through a Bucket and ensures a final flush.

      Caveats:

      • In parallel streams, encounter order is not guaranteed by this collector’s simple combiner.
      • This collector batches by size only. For modern JDKs, Gatherers.windowFixed(maxSize) is usually the more idiomatic choice for pure stream pipelines.
      Typparameter:
      A - the element type
      Parameter:
      maxSize - the maximum batch size; must be >= 1
      sink - the sink invoked with each flushed batch; must not be null
      Gibt zurück:
      a collector that batches elements into the given sink via an internal Bucket
      Löst aus:
      IllegalArgumentException - if maxSize < 1
      NullPointerException - if sink == null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • add

      public void add(@NonNull A element)

      Adds an element to the bucket. When the bucket reaches maxSize, the current batch is flushed to the sink and the bucket is cleared.

      Concurrency: acquires the write lock. If the flush threshold is reached, flush() is called within the same critical section.

      Parameter:
      element - the element to add; must not be null
      Löst aus:
      NullPointerException - if element == null
      Seit:
      1.0.0

    • flush

      public void flush()

      Flushes any currently buffered elements to the sink and clears the bucket.

      Implementation notes:

      • This method holds the write lock while copying the current batch and while invoking the sink.
      • If the sink can block or is slow, consider an alternative design that copies under the lock, releases the lock, and only then invokes the sink.
